questions.stem: A sum of money placed at compound interest doubles itself in \(4\) years. In how many years will it amount to \(8\) times the original sum?
questions.keySolution:
The sum becomes \(2\) times in \(4\) years.
To reach \(8 = 2^3\) times, multiply the base period by \(3\).
Required time \(= 3 \times 4 = 12\) years.

questions.stem: A certain sum becomes \(3\) times itself in \(6\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(27\) times?
questions.keySolution:
Multiplier \(=3\) in \(6\) years.
Required multiplier \(= 27 = 3^3\).
Time \(= 3 \times 6 = 18\) years.

questions.stem: If a sum becomes \(4\) times in \(2\) years at compound interest, in how many years will it become \(16\) times?
questions.keySolution:
Given \(4 = 2^2\) in \(2\) years.
Required \(16 = 2^4\).
Exponent ratio \(\tfrac{4}{2} = 2\).
Time \(= 2 \times 2 = 4\) years.

questions.stem: A sum becomes \(9\) times in \(8\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(729\) times?
At what annual rate (compounded yearly) will a sum become \(4\) times itself in \(2\) years?
A sum amounts to \(8\) times in \(3\) years at compound interest. What is the ratio of the amount after \(1\) year to the original principal?
questions.keySolution:
Multiplier in \(3\) years \(= 8 = 2^3\).
Thus \(1+\tfrac{r}{100} = 2\).
After \(1\) year amount \(= 2P\).
Ratio \(= 2P:P = 2:1\).

questions.stem: A sum becomes \(5\) times in \(4\) years on compound interest. In how many years will it become \(125\) times?
A sum doubles itself in \(6\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(4\) times?
questions.keySolution:
Multiplier \(2\) in \(6\) years.
For \(4 = 2^2\) times, time \(= 2 \times 6 = 12\) years.

questions.stem: At compound interest a sum becomes \(27\) times in \(3\) years. What is the annual rate of interest?
A sum becomes \(16\) times in \(8\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(4\) times?
Rs. \(10\,000\) becomes Rs. \(40\,000\) in \(4\) years at compound interest. What will be the amount after \(6\) years at the same rate?
A sum becomes \(3\) times in \(10\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(9\) times?
At what annual rate will a sum become \(9\) times itself in \(2\) years if the interest is compounded annually?
A sum becomes \(6\) times in \(5\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(216\) times?
If a sum doubles in \(5\) years at compound interest, what is the ratio of compound interest to principal after \(10\) years?
questions.keySolution:
Amount after \(10\) years \(= 2^2 = 4P\).
Compound interest \(= 4P - P = 3P\).
Required ratio \(= 3P : P = 3:1\).

questions.stem: A sum becomes \(7\) times in \(6\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(343\) times?
At compound interest a sum becomes \(8\) times in \(6\) years. What is the approximate annual rate of interest?
A sum becomes \(25\) times in \(4\) years on compound interest. In how many years will it become \(125\) times?
questions.keySolution:
\(25 = 5^2\) and \(125 = 5^3\).
Time factor \(= \tfrac{3}{2}\).
Required time \(= \tfrac{3}{2} \times 4 = 6\) years.

questions.stem: Rs. \(5\,000\) becomes Rs. \(20\,000\) in \(2\) years at compound interest. What principal will amount to Rs. \(80\,000\) in \(3\) years at the same rate?
questions.keySolution:
Growth factor in \(2\) years \(= \tfrac{20\,000}{5\,000} = 4\).
Hence \(1 + \tfrac{r}{100} = 2\).
Multiplier for \(3\) years \(= 2^3 = 8\).
Required principal \(= \tfrac{80\,000}{8} = 10\,000\).

questions.stem: A sum becomes \(10\) times in \(5\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(1\,000\) times?
At what annual rate will a sum become \(16\) times itself in \(4\) years when compounded yearly?
A sum becomes \(64\) times in \(6\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(4\) times?
If a sum triples itself in \(5\) years, what is the ratio of compound interest to principal after \(10\) years?
questions.keySolution:
Amount after \(10\) years \(= 3^2 = 9P\).
Compound interest \(= 9P - P = 8P\).
Ratio \(= 8P : P = 8:1\).

questions.stem: A sum becomes \(32\) times in \(10\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become double?
questions.keySolution:
\(32 = 2^5\) in \(10\) years.
Each exponent \(1\) corresponds to \(\tfrac{10}{5}=2\) years.
Hence doubling time \(= 2\) years.

questions.stem: At what annual rate will a sum become \(125\) times in \(3\) years, compounded yearly?
A sum becomes \(12\) times in \(4\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it amount to \(144\) times?
If Rs. \(1\,000\) becomes Rs. \(8\,000\) in \(3\) years at compound interest, what will be the amount after \(4\) years at the same rate?
A sum becomes \(81\) times in \(8\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(9\) times?
questions.keySolution:
\(81 = 9^2\) in \(8\) years.
Time to reach \(9 = 9^1\): \(\tfrac{1}{2} \times 8 = 4\) years.

questions.stem: At what annual rate will a sum become \(8\) times itself in \(3\) years at compound interest?
A sum becomes \(36\) times in \(4\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(6\) times?
questions.keySolution:
\(36 = 6^2\) in \(4\) years.
Time for \(6^1\) times \(= \tfrac{1}{2} \times 4 = 2\) years.

questions.stem: If a sum becomes \(243\) times in \(5\) years at compound interest, what will it become in \(2\) years?
questions.keySolution:
\(243 = 3^5\).
So \(1+\tfrac{r}{100} = 3\).
After \(2\) years amount \(= 3^2 P = 9P\).
Hence it becomes \(9\) times.

questions.stem: A sum becomes \(100\) times in \(4\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(10\) times?
questions.keySolution:
\(100 = 10^2\) in \(4\) years.
Time for \(10^1\) times \(= \tfrac{1}{2} \times 4 = 2\) years.

questions.stem: At compound interest, if a sum becomes \(64\) times in \(3\) years, what is the annual rate of interest?
A sum becomes \(49\) times in \(6\) years at compound interest. In how many years will it become \(7\) times?
questions.keySolution:
\(49 = 7^2\) in \(6\) years.
Time for \(7\) times \(= \tfrac{1}{2} \times 6 = 3\) years.
